stage1.impression: Two pure-red acrylic monitors on speckled plinths flank a rainbow neon gyroscope globe in a dark oak-slat box. It reads as a specific room, not a generic bar, because the globe and the red pair are distinctive. But at 1:1 it is a CG render. The slat walls are uniform with no grain, the plinths read as oversized granite chips rather than honed terrazzo, the red has no tonal range, the globe's saturated rainbow rims fight the speakers for hero status, and the floor and foreground chair fall into murk with no sign of life. A design magazine would not run it as a photograph yet.

blocking_9: The left Tropos face (region 120,330,345,615) reads at lum_median >= 45 with visible tonal range in the red (g_median > 12), not a flat saturated red
The terrazzo plinths read as honed terrazzo at real chip scale (5-15 mm chips, lighter ground), and their faces are not sunk in shadow (median >= 22)
The oak slat walls show board-to-board tone and grain variation, and no wall area reads as a single repeated texture
There is a sign of life in the frame: a glass, a record out of its sleeve, or a lit lounge chair and rug that reads
The foreground is resolved: the chair arm at the bottom edge is either composed in deliberately or out of frame, and the rug reads
The globe's saturated rims stay secondary to the pair (fixed product, so the light and camera have to handle this; see out_of_scope)
Frame lum_median 24-35 with clipping < 0.5% outside the practicals

defects.what: The left speaker is underlit (lum_median 18.2) and its red is gamut-crushed (r 66 / g 3 / b 1). It reads as flat neon red, and its internal light bars clip (2.5%).
The right speaker has the same crushed red (g_median 8) and 3.7% clipping on its internal bars. It is brighter than the left one, so the pair's lighting is unbalanced.
The globe's rims are saturated rainbow (blue, green, pink, yellow). This is the frame's strongest colour and it competes with the speakers.
The left plinth reads as coarse granite: chips are too large and uniform, the ground is dark, and the face is dim (median 13). The aggregate pattern looks procedural.
The right plinth has the same coarse granite read (median 15.8).
Mother's plinth is crushed into shadow (median 11.8, crush 8.75%).
The oak slat walls are uniform and repeating, with no grain or board-to-board variation, so they read as a CG texture.
The lid and upper wall are an undifferentiated dark brown band (median 14.5) with nothing to read.
The globe's coloured shadow on the floor is a faint washed-out pink, green and beige ellipse that reads as a rug or a stain, not as coloured light.
The end-grain floor shows no end-grain. It is a smooth brown plane with red spill on the left.
The foreground lounge chair arm is a soft, unlit blob cutting into the bottom edge. It reads as an accident.
A cropped side table or chair at the bottom right is a tangent at the frame edge.
There are no props or signs of life. The room reads as a showroom.

changes.problem: The Tropos pair, the hero, is underlit on its face and unbalanced left to right, so the left speaker reads as a dark red silhouette.

evidence.measured: Left lum_median 18.2 against a target of 45 or more. Right [850,340,1000,560] lum_median 31.1. The y profile drops from 159 at the top bar to 10-30 on the body.

change.setting: inside the lantern: the pair 2 x spot
change.to: 95 W, 30 deg, 3000 K, re-aimed at each speaker's front baffle from about 30 deg above the camera axis, with the left spot ~1.3x the right to balance the pair

changes.expected: Both speaker faces read with a gradient from lit baffle to darker sides. The left face's median rises to ~45-55.

changes.problem: The Ember acrylic is rendered as channel-clipped pure red, which reads as plastic or signage rather than a tinted cast block.

evidence.measured: r_median 66, g_median 3, b_median 1, clip 2.52% on the internal bars

change.from: white_balance_k 3200, look AgX - Medium High Contrast
change.to: white_balance_k 2850, look AgX - Base Contrast (or Medium Contrast)

changes.expected: The red keeps its hue but gains tonal range and warm-orange body (g_median rises above 12). The bars' clipping falls, and the room's timber goes from orange to warm brown.

changes.problem: The plinths and lower room fall into shadow, so the frame sits just under its target and the plinths do not read as material.

evidence.measured: Left plinth median 13.2, Mother's plinth [450,530,630,645] median 11.8 with crush 8.75%, frame lum_p50 20.0

change.setting: inside the lantern: the trap 1 x area and fill 1 x area
change.to: trap 0.45 W/m2 grazing low across the plinth faces, fill 0.07 W/m2

changes.expected: The plinth faces read at a median of ~22-30 and the frame median lands at 24-30. The shadows hold detail while the room stays dark.

changes.problem: The terrazzo reads as coarse granite: the chips are oversized and uniform on a dark ground.

evidence.measured: At 1:1 the chips are ~6-10 px across, about 30-50 mm at this distance, and evenly spread with no matrix showing.

change.setting: terrazzo chip size and ground tone
change.to: chips 5-15 mm with size variation, a warm grey cement ground ~2 stops lighter, a honed low-sheen finish with a faint roughness variation

changes.expected: The plinths read as honed terrazzo and their median rises further. The aggregate stops reading as procedural noise.

changes.problem: The globe sits dead centre at the speakers' height and its rainbow rims take the eye from the pair. The foreground chair arm cuts the bottom edge as a blur.

evidence.measured: The globe's rims are the frame's most saturated area (lum_p95 156), centred. The chair arm blob [160,740,600,800] is unlit at median 17.

change.to: Move ~0.6 m toward the left speaker's side and raise to 1.2 m (seated eye) at 40 mm, so the near Tropos is large in the left third and the globe falls back behind and right of centre. Either bring the chair arm and rug clearly into the lower left or exclude them.

changes.expected: One speaker is the clear hero and the globe is a secondary element. The bottom edge is clean.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life, so the room reads as a showroom rather than a listening bar at night.

evidence.measured: Visual: no glass, record or coat anywhere in the frame. The rug and lounge chairs barely register.

change.to: A tumbler with a finger of whisky and a record sleeve leaning on the near lounge chair or a low side table in the lower left, caught by a narrow 2700 K spot. The rug lit enough to read.

changes.expected: A warm highlight on glass and paper in the foreground gives scale and life.

changes.problem: The oak slat walls and lid are uniform and repeat, which is the main 'render' tell in the background.

evidence.measured: lum_range 47 with an even stripe pattern, no grain at 1:1. Top band [0,0,1200,180] median 14.5, range 25.

change.to: Per-slat random tone offset of ±8% and hue variation, visible flat-sawn grain, and a slight sheen variation from the oil finish

changes.expected: The walls read as real oiled oak boards, and the lid gains visible board structure.

changes.problem: The air is perfectly clear, so the spots form no pools or beams and the room lacks atmosphere.

evidence.measured: The upper frame is flat at median 14.5, with no beam structure visible above the speakers or the globe.

changes.expected: A faint visible cone above Mother EARF and the pair, and a softer falloff into the lid. The frame's upper band lifts slightly.

out_of_scope.request: Make Mother EARF's rims a single tint, or dim her rim glow, so the speaker pair is the only saturated colour in the frame
out_of_scope.why: Mother EARF's six tinted discs and glowing rims are a fixed product. The 'one colour' criterion conflicts with the card, so it can only be eased through the camera (c5) and the grade.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Tropos acrylic thicker and edge-glowing, with less dense red tint
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's material and tint are the product and are fixed.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the plinth stone or the oak slat wall design
out_of_scope.why: Terrazzo and oak are fixed materials. Only their finish and tone may change (c4, c7).
